ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.RandomEnemy)` (SwordBoomerang.cs:19-22) == cost 1 / ATTACK / COMMON / RANDOM_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(3m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new RepeatVar(3)` (SwordBoomerang.cs:13-17) == both numbers, and `base_hits` reports 3.

OnPlay.rationale: THE STREAM IS HANDLED CORRECTLY HERE, unlike card/rip_and_tear, which does the same thing on the shared rng. C#'s `TargetingRandomOpponents(CombatState)` re-rolls `(Attacker.Player ?? Attacker.PetOwner).RunState.Rng.CombatTargets.NextItem(validTargets)` per hit (AttackCommand.cs:601-602) with `allowDuplicates` defaulting true (309, 325, 72) and `validTargets` re-derived from `where c.IsAlive` at the top of each hit (544-546). The sim branches on `crng.is_parity` and uses `crng.targets.choice(living)` (sword_boomerang.py:289-292), keeping the shared legacy rng only for non-parity RL runs, with the AttackCommand.cs:601-602 citation in-line; the per-hit `living` rebuild and the duplicates-allowed independent choice both match. This makes sword_boomerang a FALSE POSITIVE in the `shared-rng` probe's list of 21 -- like card/alchemize, its `combat._rng` use is the legacy branch only.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Repeat.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` (SwordBoomerang.cs:34) == `self._hits += 1` (3 -> 4). The damage stays 3 per hit when upgraded on both sides.

guards.what: the sim also breaks the hit loop on `ctx.player.is_dead` (sword_boomerang.py:287-288)
guards.rationale: C# breaks on `Attacker.IsDead` at the top of each hit (AttackCommand.cs:540-543), so this is the same guard, not an addition.
